hypotheses.reasoning: Traffic was healthy up to 13:03 with the cache hitting at about 98% (#146). At 13:03:17 redis-cache restarted after a node replacement with no RDB snapshot and 0 keys (#157). Almost immediately search-api saw a 97% miss ratio and fell through to catalog-db (#158, #163). The resulting stampede saturated catalog-db (connections 490/500, CPU 99%, #162) and made simple PK lookups slow (#164). That caused search-api query timeouts (#171) and web-bff 504s (#172). The cold-cache stampede cascaded onto the DB; web-bff and search-api are downstream symptoms.
The immediate failing resource is the catalog-db connection pool and CPU, which are saturated (#162, #174). But this exhaustion was triggered by the cache cold start, not by growth in load.

verdict.recommendedAction: Warm the redis cache: pre-load hot product keys from catalog-db at a controlled rate. Turn on request coalescing or single-flight for cache misses in search-api, and rate-limit or shed load to catalog-db until the hit ratio recovers. Afterwards, enable RDB/AOF persistence or replicas for redis so that replacing a node doesn't bring it back with an empty cache, and add stampede protection such as jittered TTLs and probabilistic early refresh.
